title: The Role of Cash Register Machines on Tax Collection Efficiency in Addis Ketema Sub‐City, Addis Ababa‐Ethiopia
content: This study assesses the efficiency of Cash Register Machines (CRMs) in tax collection, focusing on the Addis Ketema Sub-City Tax Office in Ethiopia. Despite government efforts to modernize tax administration through CRM adoption, challenges related to technical maintenance, taxpayer awareness, and operational costs persist. Using an explanatory research design with a mixed-methods approach, data were collected via questionnaires from 347 taxpayers and interviews with six tax office experts. The analysis employed descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. The findings reveal a strong positive correlation (R=0.871) between the predictors and tax collection, with the model explaining 75.8% of the variance in tax collection (R²=0.758). Tax audit follow-up (β=0.684, p<0.001) and taxpayer knowledge and awareness (β=0.257, p<0.001) were the most significant predictors. The study concludes that CRMs are potent tools for enhancing tax efficiency but their effectiveness is moderated by robust audit systems, continuous taxpayer education, and reliable technical support. Recommendations include intensifying awareness campaigns, improving audit transparency, strengthening supplier maintenance protocols, and resolving technical connectivity issues to maximize CRM benefits.
